subject: math
title: Similar Shapes and Scale Diagrams: Scale Factors, Missing Sides, Maps and Shadows
seo_title: Grade 9 Similar Shapes and Scale Diagrams Worksheets (BC Math): Free with Answer Key
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 math worksheets on similar shapes and scale diagrams for the BC curriculum: scale factors, missing sides in similar triangles, enlargements and reductions, maps and plans, and shadow problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Similar shapes have equal angles and proportional sides: multiply every length by the same scale factor. Never add.
key_sub: Scale factor = new length ÷ original length. Match the sides first: in △ABC ~ △DEF, AB matches DE.
body_html:
What makes shapes similar

Two shapes are similar when they have the same shape but maybe a different size. Matching angles are equal. Matching sides are in proportion: every side is multiplied by the same number.

That number is the scale factor. Scale factor = new length ÷ original length. A scale factor greater than 1 is an enlargement. A scale factor between 0 and 1 is a reduction.

Find the scale factor

A 4 cm side becomes 10 cm. What is the scale factor?

10 ÷ 4 = 2.5. Every other side is also multiplied by 2.5.

Answer: 2.5

Missing sides in similar triangles

First match the sides. In △ABC ~ △DEF, the letters match in order: A ↔ D, B ↔ E, C ↔ F. Then find the scale factor from one known pair, and multiply.

Use a proportion

△ABC ~ △DEF. AB = 4 cm, BC = 6 cm and DE = 10 cm. Find EF.

EF ÷ BC = DE ÷ AB, so EF ÷ 6 = 10 ÷ 4. EF = 6 × 2.5.

Answer: 15 cm

Scale diagrams, maps and plans

A scale diagram is similar to the real object. Diagram length = scale factor × real length. To go back to the real length, divide. On a map, 1:50 000 means 1 cm stands for 50 000 cm, which is 500 m.

Shadows and heights

At the same time of day, the sun’s rays make similar right triangles. Height ÷ shadow is the same for every object.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
4 cm → 6 cm, so 10 cm → 12 cm (adding 2)Multiply: 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5, and 10 × 1.5 = 15 cm
Matching sides by where they sit on the pageMatch by the letters (AB ↔ DE) or by the angles
Using DB instead of the whole side ABIn nested triangles, AB = AD + DB
Dividing by the scale factor to find the new sideNew side = original × scale factor
1:50 000, so 4 cm is 200 000 m200 000 cm = 2000 m = 2 km

faq.q: What do Grade 9 students learn about similar shapes in BC?
faq.a: Mathematics 9 in BC includes spatial proportional reasoning: students use scale factors, similar triangles and scale diagrams to find missing lengths, and solve problems with maps, plans and shadows.

faq.q: How can you tell if two shapes are similar?
faq.a: Their matching angles are equal and the ratios of their matching sides are all the same. For rectangles, check that length ÷ length equals width ÷ width.

faq.q: How do you find a missing side in similar triangles?
faq.a: Match the sides, find the scale factor from one known pair (new ÷ original), then multiply the matching side by it. Do not add the difference.

faq.q: How do you find the height of a tree with shadows?
faq.a: Measure a person or stick and its shadow at the same time as the tree’s shadow. Height ÷ shadow is the same for both, so tree height = tree shadow × (person’s height ÷ person’s shadow).

items.q: Two figures are similar. Which statement is always true?
c: Angles are equal; sides are in proportion
Angles and sides are all equal
Sides are equal; angles are in proportion
Every side is longer by the same amount
items.e: Similar figures have the same shape: matching angles are equal, and every side is multiplied by the same scale factor. Equal sides would make the figures congruent, and adding the same amount changes the shape.

items.q: The small rectangle is enlarged to make the large one. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Scale factor = new length ÷ original length = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 (check: 9 ÷ 3 = 3). 4 is the difference 6 − 2, and 13 divides the wrong way.

items.q: The triangles are similar. What scale factor takes the green triangle to the blue triangle?
items.e: Matching sides: 8 ÷ 4 = 2, 10 ÷ 5 = 2, 12 ÷ 6 = 2. The scale factor is 2. 4 is the difference 8 − 4, and 12 takes the blue triangle back to the green one.

items.q: The green triangle is reduced to make the blue triangle. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Scale factor = new ÷ original = 8 ÷ 16 = 0.5. A reduction always has a scale factor less than 1. 2 divides the wrong way, and 8 and 6 are differences (16 − 8 and 12 − 6), not a factor.

items.q: A side of a figure is 6 cm long. The figure is enlarged by a scale factor of 3. How long is the new side?
items.e: Multiply by the scale factor: 6 × 3 = 18 cm. 9 cm adds 3, 2 cm divides by 3, and 3 cm subtracts 3.

items.q: A side is 14 cm long. The figure is reduced by a scale factor of 0.5. How long is the new side?
items.e: 14 × 0.5 = 7 cm. 28 cm divides by 0.5, and 14.5 cm and 13.5 cm add or subtract 0.5.

items.q: A triangle has angles 50°, 60° and 70°. It is enlarged by a scale factor of 2. What is the angle that matches the 60° angle?
items.e: Enlarging changes the side lengths, not the angles. Matching angles are equal, so it is still 60°. 120° doubles the angle, which would make the angle sum 360°, not 180°.

items.q: Are these two rectangles similar?
c: Yes: both sides grow by 2 cm
items.e: Check the ratios of matching sides: 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5 but 8 ÷ 6 ≈ 1.33. They are not equal, so the rectangles are not similar. Adding 2 cm to each side keeps the same difference, not the same shape.

items.q: Are these two rectangles similar?
c: No: the sides grow by different amounts
items.e: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5 and 15 ÷ 6 = 2.5. The ratios are equal, so the rectangles are similar with scale factor 2.5. The sides grow by 6 cm and 9 cm, but similar figures multiply; they do not add.

items.q: Which rectangle is similar to a 3 cm by 5 cm rectangle?
items.e: 9 ÷ 3 = 3 and 15 ÷ 5 = 3, so 9 cm by 15 cm is similar. 5 by 7 and 6 by 8 add to both sides, and 6 by 15 multiplies the sides by different numbers (2 and 3).

items.q: Which triangle is similar to a triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm?
items.e: Every side must be multiplied by the same number: 3 × 2 = 6, 4 × 2 = 8, 5 × 2 = 10, so 6 cm, 8 cm, 10 cm. 4, 5, 6 adds 1 to each side; the other two multiply only some sides.

items.q: △ABC ~ △DEF. Which side matches side AB?
items.e: The order of the letters tells you the match: A ↔ D, B ↔ E, C ↔ F. So AB matches DE. The blue triangle is flipped, so do not match sides by where they sit on the page.

items.q: △ABC ~ △DEF. Which angle is equal to ∠B?
items.e: In △ABC ~ △DEF, the second letters match: B ↔ E. So ∠B = ∠E.

items.q: △PQR ~ △STU. Which ratio is equal to PQST?
items.e: Match the letters in order: P ↔ S, Q ↔ T, R ↔ U. So PQ/ST = QR/TU = PR/SU, and the answer is QR/TU. The other ratios pair sides that do not match.

items.q: An original side is 15 cm. The matching side of the image is 6 cm. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Scale factor = image ÷ original = 6 ÷ 15 = 0.4. 2.5 divides the wrong way, 9 is the difference, and 0.6 is 9 ÷ 15 (the difference divided by the original).

items.q: A side is 9 cm long. The figure is enlarged by a scale factor of 1.5. How long is the new side?
items.e: 9 × 1.5 = 13.5 cm. 10.5 cm adds 1.5, 7.5 cm subtracts 1.5, and 6 cm divides by 1.5.

items.q: A side is 12 cm long. The figure is reduced by a scale factor of 23. How long is the new side?
items.e: 12 × 23 = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 cm. 18 cm divides by 23, 4 cm finds only 13 of 12, and 36 cm multiplies by 3.

items.q: A figure is changed with a scale factor of 0.75. What is the new figure?
items.e: A scale factor between 0 and 1 makes every side shorter, so the image is a reduction. A scale factor greater than 1 enlarges, and a scale factor of 1 gives a congruent copy.

items.q: Two triangles are similar with a scale factor of 3. The small triangle has a perimeter of 15 cm. What is the perimeter of the large triangle?
items.e: Every side is multiplied by 3, so the perimeter is too: 15 × 3 = 45 cm. 18 cm adds 3, 24 cm adds 3 to each of the 3 sides, and 135 cm multiplies by 9 (that is for area).

items.q: A 4 cm by 10 cm rectangle is similar to a 6 cm by x cm rectangle. The 4 cm side matches the 6 cm side. What is x?
items.e: Scale factor: 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5. x = 10 × 1.5 = 15. 12 adds 2, 2.4 is 6 × 4 ÷ 10 (sides matched the wrong way), and 16 adds 6.

items.q: The triangles are similar. Find x.
items.e: Matching sides: 6 cm and 12 cm. Scale factor: 12 ÷ 6 = 2. x = 5 × 2 = 10 cm. 11 cm adds 6 (the difference 12 − 6) instead of multiplying, 8 cm scales the wrong side (4 cm), and 2.5 cm divides by the scale factor instead of multiplying.

items.q: The triangles are similar. Find x.
items.e: Matching sides: 4 cm and 8 cm. Scale factor: 8 ÷ 4 = 2. x = 5 × 2 = 10 cm. 9 cm adds 4 (the difference 8 − 4) instead of multiplying, 6 cm scales the wrong side (3 cm), and 2.5 cm divides by the scale factor instead of multiplying.

items.q: The triangles are similar. Find x.
items.e: Matching sides: 12 cm and 6 cm. Scale factor: 6 ÷ 12 = 0.5. x = 8 × 0.5 = 4 cm. 2 cm subtracts 6 (the difference 12 − 6) instead of multiplying, 5 cm scales the wrong side (10 cm), and 16 cm divides by the scale factor instead of multiplying.

items.q: The triangles are similar. Find x.
items.e: Matching sides: 4 cm and 10 cm. Scale factor: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5. x = 5 × 2.5 = 12.5 cm. 11 cm adds 6 (the difference 10 − 4) instead of multiplying, 15 cm scales the wrong side (6 cm), and 2 cm divides by the scale factor instead of multiplying.

items.q: The triangles are similar. Find x.
items.e: Matching sides: 2 m and 6 m. Scale factor: 6 ÷ 2 = 3. x = 3 × 3 = 9 m. 7 m adds 4 (the difference 6 − 2) instead of multiplying, 12 m scales the wrong side (4 m), and 1 m divides by the scale factor instead of multiplying.

items.q: The triangles are similar. Find x.
items.e: Matching sides: 6 cm and 12 cm. Scale factor: 12 ÷ 6 = 2. x = 7 × 2 = 14 cm. 13 cm adds 6 (the difference 12 − 6) instead of multiplying, 10 cm scales the wrong side (5 cm), and 3.5 cm divides by the scale factor instead of multiplying.

items.q: △ABC ~ △DEF. AB = 4 cm, BC = 6 cm and DE = 10 cm. How long is EF?
items.e: AB matches DE, and BC matches EF. Scale factor: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5. EF = 6 × 2.5 = 15 cm. 12 cm adds 6, 25 cm scales DE instead of BC, and 2.4 cm divides by 2.5.

items.q: The triangles are similar. Find x.
items.e: Matching sides: 12 cm and 8 cm. Scale factor: 8 ÷ 12 = 23. x = 9 × 23 = 6 cm. 5 cm subtracts 4 (the difference 12 − 8) instead of multiplying, 4 cm scales the wrong side (6 cm), and 13.5 cm divides by the scale factor instead of multiplying.

items.q: The triangles are similar. Find x.
items.e: Matching sides: 6 cm and 12 cm. Scale factor: 12 ÷ 6 = 2. x = 8 × 2 = 16 cm. 14 cm adds 6 (the difference 12 − 6) instead of multiplying, 20 cm scales the wrong side (10 cm), and 4 cm divides by the scale factor instead of multiplying.

items.q: The triangles are similar. Find x.
items.e: Matching sides: 4 cm and 10 cm. Scale factor: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5. x = 3 × 2.5 = 7.5 cm. 9 cm adds 6 (the difference 10 − 4) instead of multiplying, 15 cm scales the wrong side (6 cm), and 1.2 cm divides by the scale factor instead of multiplying.

items.q: DE is parallel to BC, so △ADE ~ △ABC. Find x.
items.e: AB = 6 + 3 = 9. Scale factor: AB ÷ AD = 9 ÷ 6. x = 8 × 9 ÷ 6 = 12 cm. 4 cm matches DE with DB instead of using the whole side AB, 11 cm adds DB instead of multiplying, and 24 cm uses DB in place of AD.

items.q: The triangles are similar. Find x.
items.e: Matching sides: 8 cm and 10 cm. Scale factor: 10 ÷ 8 = 1.25. x = 10 × 1.25 = 12.5 cm. 12 cm adds 2 (the difference 10 − 8) instead of multiplying, 7.5 cm scales the wrong side (6 cm), and 8 cm divides by the scale factor instead of multiplying.

items.q: The triangles are similar. Find x.
items.e: Matching sides: 15 cm and 10 cm. Scale factor: 10 ÷ 15 = 23. x = 12 × 23 = 8 cm. 7 cm subtracts 5 (the difference 15 − 10) instead of multiplying, 6 cm scales the wrong side (9 cm), and 18 cm divides by the scale factor instead of multiplying.

items.q: DE is parallel to BC, so △ADE ~ △ABC. Find x.
items.e: AB = 5 + 10 = 15. Scale factor: AB ÷ AD = 15 ÷ 5. x = 4 × 15 ÷ 5 = 12 cm. 8 cm matches DE with DB instead of using the whole side AB, 14 cm adds DB instead of multiplying, and 6 cm uses DB in place of AD.

items.q: △PQR ~ △STU. PQ = 12 cm, QR = 9 cm and ST = 8 cm. How long is TU?
items.e: PQ matches ST, and QR matches TU. Scale factor: 8 ÷ 12 = 23. TU = 9 × 23 = 6 cm. 5 cm subtracts 4, 13.5 cm multiplies by 1.5 (the wrong way), and 4 cm is 12 − 8.

items.q: The triangles are similar. Find x.
items.e: Matching sides: 5 cm and 7 cm. Scale factor: 7 ÷ 5 = 1.4. x = 7 × 1.4 = 9.8 cm. 9 cm adds 2 (the difference 7 − 5) instead of multiplying, 8.4 cm scales the wrong side (6 cm), and 5 cm divides by the scale factor instead of multiplying.

items.q: DE is parallel to BC, so △ADE ~ △ABC. Find x.
items.e: AB = 6 + 4 = 10. Scale factor: AD ÷ AB = 6 ÷ 10. x = 15 × 6 ÷ 10 = 9 cm. 22.5 cm matches DE with DB instead of using the whole side AB, 11 cm subtracts DB instead of multiplying, and 6 cm uses DB in place of AD.

items.q: The triangles are similar. Find x.
items.e: Matching sides: 12 cm and 9 cm. Scale factor: 9 ÷ 12 = 0.75. x = 16 × 0.75 = 12 cm. 13 cm subtracts 3 (the difference 12 − 9) instead of multiplying, 6 cm scales the wrong side (8 cm), and 18 cm matches sides by their place on the page, not by shape.

items.q: DE is parallel to BC, so △ADE ~ △ABC. Find x.
items.e: AB = 3 + 6 = 9. Scale factor: AD ÷ AB = 3 ÷ 9. x = 12 × 3 ÷ 9 = 4 cm. 6 cm matches DE with DB instead of using the whole side AB, 8 cm uses DB in place of AD, and 36 cm multiplies by the wrong ratio.

items.q: The triangles are similar. Find x.
items.e: Matching sides: 5 cm and 8 cm. Scale factor: 8 ÷ 5 = 1.6. x = 10 × 1.6 = 16 cm. 13 cm adds 3 (the difference 8 − 5) instead of multiplying, 11.2 cm scales the wrong side (7 cm), and 6.25 cm divides by the scale factor instead of multiplying.

items.q: A scale diagram of a ladybug uses a scale factor of 5. The real ladybug is 8 mm long. How long is the ladybug in the diagram?
items.e: Diagram length = scale factor × real length = 5 × 8 = 40 mm. 13 mm adds 5, 1.6 mm divides by 5, and 3 mm subtracts 5.

items.q: What scale factor takes the original to the image?
items.e: Count squares: the width goes from 2 to 4 and the height from 3 to 6. 4 ÷ 2 = 6 ÷ 3 = 2. 3 is the change in height (6 − 3), 12 divides the wrong way, and 4 is the image width.

items.q: A scale factor of 2.5 is used to make a scale diagram. What kind of diagram is it?
items.e: 2.5 is greater than 1, so every length is multiplied by more than 1: the diagram is an enlargement.

items.q: A real feather is 30 cm long. In a scale diagram it is 6 cm long. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Scale factor = diagram length ÷ real length = 6 ÷ 30 = 0.2. 5 divides the wrong way, 24 is the difference, and 0.8 is 24 ÷ 30.

items.q: A scale diagram of an ant uses a scale factor of 4. The ant is 6 cm long in the diagram. How long is the real ant?
items.e: Real length = diagram length ÷ scale factor = 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5 cm. 24 cm multiplies, which would make the real ant bigger than the enlarged drawing. 2 cm subtracts 4, and 10 cm adds 4.

items.q: Which scale factor gives a reduction?
items.e: A reduction needs a scale factor between 0 and 1, so 0.8. 1.2 and 8 enlarge, and 1 keeps the same size.

items.q: A scale diagram of a hummingbird is 24 cm long. The real bird is 8 cm long. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Scale factor = 24 ÷ 8 = 3. 13 divides the wrong way, 16 is the difference, and 32 adds the two lengths.

items.q: A 9 cm by 12 cm photo is enlarged by a scale factor of 3. What size is the new photo?
items.e: Multiply both sides by 3: 9 × 3 = 27 and 12 × 3 = 36, so 27 cm by 36 cm. 12 by 15 adds 3, 27 by 12 enlarges only one side, and 3 by 4 divides by 3.

items.q: To enlarge a 4 cm line to 10 cm, what scale factor is needed?
items.e: Scale factor = 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5. 6 is the difference, 0.4 divides the wrong way, and 40 multiplies the lengths.

items.q: What scale factor takes the original to the image?
items.e: Width 6 → 3 and height 4 → 2. 3 ÷ 6 = 2 ÷ 4 = 0.5. 2 divides the wrong way, 3 is the change in width, and 0.25 multiplies 0.5 by itself.

items.q: A 20 cm by 30 cm picture is reduced so that the 20 cm side becomes 8 cm. How long does the 30 cm side become?
items.e: Scale factor: 8 ÷ 20 = 0.4. 30 × 0.4 = 12 cm. 18 cm subtracts 12 from both sides, 75 cm divides by 0.4, and 3.2 cm uses 0.4 twice (8 × 0.4).

items.q: What scale factor takes the original to the image?
items.e: Width 4 → 6 and height 6 → 9: 6 ÷ 4 = 9 ÷ 6 = 1.5. 2 and 3 are the changes in width and height, and 23 divides the wrong way.

items.q: A scale diagram of a bee uses a scale factor of 6. The real bee is 1.5 cm long. How long is the bee in the diagram?
items.e: 6 × 1.5 = 9 cm. 7.5 cm adds 6, 0.25 cm divides by 6, and 90 cm puts the decimal point in the wrong place.

items.q: Each 1 cm in a scale diagram stands for 4 cm in real life. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Scale factor = diagram ÷ real = 1 ÷ 4 = 0.25. The diagram is a reduction. 4 divides the wrong way, 3 is the difference, and 5 adds.

items.q: A 1.2 m long poster is reduced by a scale factor of 34. How long is the new poster?
items.e: 1.2 × 34 = 3.6 ÷ 4 = 0.9 m. 1.6 m divides by 34, 1.95 m adds 0.75, and 0.45 m subtracts 0.75.

items.q: A figure is enlarged by a scale factor of 2. The image is then enlarged by a scale factor of 3. What single scale factor takes the original to the final image?
items.e: Each step multiplies the lengths: 2 × 3 = 6. 5 adds the scale factors, 1.5 divides them, and 3 uses only the last step.

items.q: A scale diagram of a plant cell uses a scale factor of 200. The real cell is 0.05 mm across. How wide is the cell in the diagram?
items.e: 200 × 0.05 = 10 mm. 200.05 mm adds, 0.00025 mm divides by 200, and 100 mm puts the decimal point in the wrong place.

items.q: A scale diagram of a canoe uses a scale factor of 0.02. The canoe is 10 cm long in the diagram. How long is the real canoe?
items.e: Real length = 10 ÷ 0.02 = 500 cm = 5 m. 0.002 m multiplies by 0.02 (0.2 cm), and 0.5 m and 50 m slip when changing cm to m.

items.q: A model of a ferry uses a scale factor of 1200. The real ferry is 160 m long. How long is the model?
items.e: 160 m = 16 000 cm. 16 000 ÷ 200 = 80 cm. 0.8 cm and 8 cm slip when changing units, and 32 000 cm multiplies by 200.

items.q: A 4 cm by 6 cm drawing of a salmon is enlarged so that the 6 cm side becomes 15 cm. How long does the 4 cm side become?
items.e: Scale factor: 15 ÷ 6 = 2.5. 4 × 2.5 = 10 cm. 13 cm adds 9, 1.6 cm divides by 2.5, and 22.5 cm matches the sides the wrong way (15 × 6 ÷ 4).

items.q: A map has the scale 1 cm : 5 km. Two towns are 3 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they?
items.e: Each 1 cm stands for 5 km: 3 × 5 = 15 km. 8 km adds, 0.6 km divides, and 150 km multiplies by 10 too.

items.q: A map has the scale 1:50 000. Two lakes are 4 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they?
items.e: 4 × 50 000 = 200 000 cm = 2000 m = 2 km. 200 km reads the centimetres as metres; 20 km and 0.2 km slip by a factor of 10.

items.q: A road on this map is 6 cm long. How long is the real road?
items.e: The bar shows 4 cm for 20 km, so 1 cm stands for 5 km. 6 × 5 = 30 km. 120 km multiplies 6 by the whole bar, 24 km multiplies 6 by 4, and 10 km adds 6 and 4.

items.q: A floor plan has the scale 1:100. A wall is 4.5 cm long on the plan. How long is the real wall?
items.e: 4.5 × 100 = 450 cm = 4.5 m. 450 m forgets that the 450 is in centimetres; 45 m and 0.45 m slip by 10.

items.q: A plan has the scale 1:50. A bed is 4 cm long on the plan. How long is the real bed?
items.e: 4 × 50 = 200 cm = 2 m. 200 m forgets to change cm to m, 20 m slips by 10, and 54 cm adds 50.

items.q: A map has the scale 1 cm : 3 km. Two towns are 18 km apart. How far apart are they on the map?
items.e: Real to map: divide. 18 ÷ 3 = 6 cm. 54 cm multiplies, 15 cm subtracts, and 21 cm adds.

items.q: Write the scale 1 cm : 2 m as a ratio with no units.
items.e: Use the same unit for both parts: 2 m = 200 cm, so the scale is 1:200. 1:2 ignores the units, and 1:20 and 1:2000 change the units by the wrong amount.

items.q: Write the scale 1 cm : 1 km as a ratio with no units.
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m = 100 000 cm, so 1 cm : 1 km is 1:100 000. 1:1000 changes km to m but stops there.

items.q: The scale of this plan is 1:200. How long is the longer side of the real garage?
items.e: 5 × 200 = 1000 cm = 10 m. 1000 m forgets the cm, and 100 m and 1 m divide by the wrong power of 10.

items.q: The scale of this plan is 1 cm : 1.5 m. What is the area of the real patio?
items.e: Real sides: 4 × 1.5 = 6 m and 3 × 1.5 = 4.5 m. Area: 6 × 4.5 = 27 m². 18 m² multiplies the plan area by 1.5 only once, 21 is the perimeter, and 12 m² is the area on the plan.

items.q: A city map has the scale 1:20 000. Two SkyTrain stations are 6 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they?
items.e: 6 × 20 000 = 120 000 cm = 1200 m = 1.2 km. 120 km reads the cm as m; 12 km and 0.12 km slip by 10.

items.q: A trail in a park is 750 m long. How long is it on a map with the scale 1:25 000?
items.e: 750 m = 75 000 cm. 75 000 ÷ 25 000 = 3 cm. The other choices slip by powers of 10 when changing m to cm.

items.q: A 12 m wall is 6 cm long on a plan. What is the scale of the plan?
items.e: 12 m = 1200 cm. 6 cm stands for 1200 cm, so 1 cm stands for 1200 ÷ 6 = 200 cm. The scale is 1:200. 1:2 forgets to change m to cm.

items.q: Two towns 15 km apart are 5 cm apart on a map. What is the scale of the map?
items.e: 15 km = 1 500 000 cm. 1 500 000 ÷ 5 = 300 000, so the scale is 1:300 000. 1:3 forgets to change km to cm.

items.q: A lake on this map is 3.5 cm long. How long is the real lake?
items.e: The bar shows 5 cm for 10 km, so 1 cm stands for 2 km. 3.5 × 2 = 7 km. 35 km multiplies by 10, 17.5 km multiplies by 5, and 13.5 km adds 3.5 and 10.

items.q: Two towns are 8 cm apart on a road map with the scale 1:250 000. How far apart are they?
items.e: 8 × 250 000 = 2 000 000 cm = 20 000 m = 20 km. The other choices slip by powers of 10.

items.q: A house is drawn at four different scales. Which scale makes the largest drawing?
items.e: At 1:50, 1 cm stands for only 50 cm, so it takes more centimetres to draw the house. 1:50 is the largest drawing; 1:500 is the smallest.

items.q: A wall is 6 cm long on a 1:100 plan. How long is it on a 1:200 plan of the same house?
items.e: Real wall: 6 × 100 = 600 cm. At 1:200: 600 ÷ 200 = 3 cm. 12 cm multiplies by 2, 600 cm is the real length, and 1.5 cm halves twice.

items.q: A classroom is 9 m long. A student draws it 18 cm long on a plan. What is the scale?
items.e: 9 m = 900 cm. 900 ÷ 18 = 50, so 1 cm stands for 50 cm: 1:50. 1:2 ignores the units, 2:1 divides 18 by 9, and 1:500 slips by 10.

items.q: A hiking map has the scale 1:50 000. A trail is 4 km long. How long is it on the map?
items.e: 4 km = 400 000 cm. 400 000 ÷ 50 000 = 8 cm. 0.8 cm and 80 cm slip by 10, and 12.5 cm divides 50 by 4.

sets.title: Word problems: shadows, heights and models

items.q: At the same time of day, Olivia (1.5 m tall) casts a 2 m shadow and a tree casts a 12 m shadow. How tall is the tree?
items.e: The sun makes similar triangles. The tree’s shadow is 12 ÷ 2 = 6 times as long, so the tree is 1.5 × 6 = 9 m tall. 11.5 m subtracts 0.5 instead of multiplying, 16 m matches height with shadow the wrong way (12 × 2 ÷ 1.5), and 13.5 m adds 1.5 to the shadow.

items.q: A metre stick casts a 1.6 m shadow. At the same time, a flagpole casts a 12.8 m shadow. How tall is the flagpole?
items.e: Height ÷ shadow is the same for both: 1 ÷ 1.6. Flagpole: 12.8 ÷ 1.6 = 8 m. 12.2 m subtracts 0.6, 20.48 m multiplies by 1.6 instead of dividing, and 13.8 m adds 1.

items.q: A 2 m pole casts a 3 m shadow. At the same time, a western red cedar casts a 45 m shadow. How tall is the cedar?
items.e: Shadow scale factor: 45 ÷ 3 = 15. Height: 2 × 15 = 30 m. 44 m subtracts 1, 67.5 m matches the sides the wrong way (45 × 3 ÷ 2), and 47 m adds 2.

items.q: Ryan is 1.8 m tall and casts a 1.2 m shadow. A 24 m building is beside him. How long is the building’s shadow?
items.e: Shadow ÷ height = 1.2 ÷ 1.8 = 23. Building’s shadow: 24 × 23 = 16 m. 23.4 m subtracts 0.6, 36 m uses height ÷ shadow (the wrong way), and 25.2 m adds 1.2.

items.q: Ethan’s shadow is 1.2 m long. At the same time, a 3 m pole casts a 2 m shadow. How tall is Ethan?
items.e: Height ÷ shadow = 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5. Ethan: 1.2 × 1.5 = 1.8 m. 2.2 m adds 1, 0.8 m divides by 1.5, and 2.5 m is 3 − 0.5.

items.q: Liam is 150 cm tall and his shadow is 90 cm long. At the same time, a Douglas fir casts a 6 m shadow. How tall is the tree?
items.e: Change to one unit: 1.5 m and 0.9 m. Height ÷ shadow = 1.5 ÷ 0.9 = 53. Tree: 6 × 53 = 10 m. 3.6 m uses the ratio upside down, 6.6 m adds 0.6, and 1000 m mixes cm and m.

items.q: Students make two similar triangles on the bank of the Fraser River to estimate its width. In the small triangle, 8 m along the bank matches 40 m in the large triangle. The small triangle’s side across is 6 m. How wide is the river (the large triangle’s side across)?
items.e: Scale factor: 40 ÷ 8 = 5. Width: 6 × 5 = 30 m. 38 m adds 32, 1.2 m divides by 5, and 48 m multiplies 6 by 8.

items.q: A 10 cm by 15 cm photo of an orca is enlarged so the 10 cm side becomes 25 cm. How long is the other side?
items.e: Scale factor: 25 ÷ 10 = 2.5. 15 × 2.5 = 37.5 cm. 30 cm adds 15, 6 cm divides by 2.5, and 40 cm adds 25 and 15.

items.q: A model of a BC Ferries ship uses a scale factor of 1250. The model is 64 cm long. How long is the real ship?
items.e: Real length = 64 × 250 = 16 000 cm = 160 m. The other choices slip by powers of 10 when changing cm to m.

items.q: Simran is 1.6 m tall and casts a 2 m shadow. A light pole at the soccer field casts a 15 m shadow. How tall is the light pole?
items.e: Scale factor: 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5. Height: 1.6 × 7.5 = 12 m. 14.6 m subtracts 0.4, 18.75 m matches the sides the wrong way (15 × 2 ÷ 1.6), and 16.6 m adds 1.6.

items.q: A model car is built at a scale of 1:24. The model is 18 cm long. How long is the real car?
items.e: 18 × 24 = 432 cm = 4.32 m. 0.75 cm divides by 24, 42 cm adds 24, and 43.2 m slips by 10.

items.q: A drawing of a salmon is 12 cm long. It is enlarged for a school mural with a scale factor of 15. How long is the salmon on the mural?
items.e: 12 × 15 = 180 cm = 1.8 m. 27 cm adds 15, 0.8 cm divides by 15, and 18 m slips when changing cm to m.

items.q: A scale diagram of a snowboard uses a scale factor of 18. The real snowboard is 152 cm long. How long is it in the diagram?
items.e: 152 × 18 = 152 ÷ 8 = 19 cm. 1216 cm multiplies by 8, and 144 cm and 160 cm subtract or add 8.

items.q: On a trail map with the scale 1:50 000, Owen’s hike near Whistler is 9 cm long. He hikes at 3 km per hour. How long does the hike take?
items.e: Distance: 9 × 50 000 = 450 000 cm = 4.5 km. Time: 4.5 ÷ 3 = 1.5 hours. 3 hours uses 9 km, 15 hours uses 45 km, and 4.5 is the distance, not the time.

items.q: A 1.2 m stick casts a 0.8 m shadow. At the same time, Kai’s shadow is 1.2 m long. How tall is Kai?
items.e: Height ÷ shadow = 1.2 ÷ 0.8 = 1.5. Kai: 1.2 × 1.5 = 1.8 m. 1.6 m adds 0.4, 0.8 m uses the ratio upside down, and 2 m adds 1.2 and 0.8.

items.q: A wheelchair ramp rises 0.6 m over a horizontal distance of 4.8 m. How high is the ramp 1.6 m from its bottom end?
items.e: The small triangle is similar to the whole ramp. Scale factor: 1.6 ÷ 4.8 = 13. Height: 0.6 × 13 = 0.2 m. 1.8 m multiplies by 3, 0.6 m is the full height, and 0.8 m halves 1.6 instead of using the scale factor.

items.q: Nadia is 1.6 m tall and casts a 2 m shadow. At the same time, a tree casts an 8 m shadow. How much taller than Nadia is the tree?
items.e: Tree: 1.6 × (8 ÷ 2) = 6.4 m. Difference: 6.4 − 1.6 = 4.8 m. 6.4 m is the tree’s full height, 6 m is 8 − 2 (shadows subtracted), and 8 m is the tree’s shadow.

items.q: A 1:100 plan of a school garden shows a vegetable bed 3.5 cm by 2 cm. Wooden edging costs $6 per metre. How much does edging for the whole bed cost?
items.e: Real sides: 3.5 m and 2 m. Perimeter: 2 × (3.5 + 2) = 11 m. Cost: 11 × $6 = $66. $33 uses only two sides, $42 multiplies the area 7 m² by $6, and $6600 forgets to change cm to m.

items.q: A photo of Grouse Mountain is 12 cm wide. It is reduced so that it fits a 9 cm wide space. The photo was 8 cm tall. How tall is it now?
items.e: Scale factor: 9 ÷ 12 = 0.75. 8 × 0.75 = 6 cm. 5 cm subtracts 3, 13.5 cm is 9 × 12 ÷ 8 (sides matched the wrong way), and 6.75 cm multiplies 9 by 0.75.

items.q: Two similar triangular sails have matching sides of 2 m and 5 m. The small sail’s longest side is 3.2 m. How long is the large sail’s longest side?
items.e: Scale factor: 5 ÷ 2 = 2.5. 3.2 × 2.5 = 8 m. 6.2 m adds 3, 1.28 m divides by 2.5, and 16 m multiplies by 5 only.
